short_answer: Spartan is a real, long running seller on Pregame, a Las Vegas pick store run by Pregame, LLC. His bio says he is a lifetime Missouri resident who placed his first bet in 1971 and spent over a decade as a local bookie. He sells single plays, season passes and subscriptions with published prices. In that narrow sense the service is legitimate.

Whether his picks make money is a separate question, and Pregame's own numbers are not flattering right now. His sales page leads with "NFL Triple Stars 2012-2026 277-183". But Pregame's graded table for the current season, rated picks only, showed 488 wins, 492 losses and 10 ties across all sports on 17 Nov 2026, with a weighted dollar loss in college football, baseball and hockey. The last 30 days were 79 and 76.

Independent buyer comment is almost absent. The praise we found is from 2012 on Pregame's own forum, and no buyer complaint turned up. Treat Spartan as a seller with one strong marketed category and an overall record near break even before the price of the picks.

guarantee: Pregame does not offer a money back or profit guarantee on his picks, and it says so on purpose. Its discount page calls "guaranteed picks" a "deceptive marketing ploy" and says the amount a bettor risks is always much bigger than the cost of the pick. That point is fair: a pick guarantee never covers the money you bet.

The one remedy we could read is opposite side insurance. The Pregame FAQ says to message support if you bought plays from two handicappers who took opposite sides of the same game, and links to the details. It is account credit, not cash. Flex Access rebills every month until you cancel by email.

claims_note: The headline numbers cover his top rated NFL plays and a few chosen categories. Pregame's full graded tables tell a different story for the current season: rated picks across all sports were 488 and 492, and the weighted dollar figures were negative in college football, baseball, hockey, college basketball and the UFL.

In Mar 2026 a forum member reposted one of his college basketball plays along with a season college basketball line of 77 and 98 and 1. That is a losing season by count, from a line that traveled with his own play.
record: What a buyer can check: Pregame grades every rated pick and shows tables by sport and period. On 17 Nov 2026, the current season table for rated picks showed MLB 351 and 345 (weighted minus $2,363), college football 56 and 62 with 5 ties (minus $2,913), NFL 47 and 43 with 3 ties (plus $319), NBA 19 and 17 (plus $7), NHL 9 and 12 (minus $512), college basketball 2 and 5 (minus $350), CFL 4 and 3 (plus $38) and UFL 0 and 5 (minus $1,034). Added up, that is 488 wins and 492 losses with a weighted loss of about $6,808.

The last 30 days, rated picks only, were 79 wins, 76 losses and 1 tie, with a weighted loss of about $1,196. The page does not say what one unit equals in dollars, so read the dollar figures as Pregame's scale, not your own money.
These tables are kept by the store that sells the picks, so they are not an independent audit. They are still more than most sellers show, and they are the best record we found.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition no Spartan pick history is matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how Spartan performs.
our_data.context: For scale: his marketed NFL Triple Star run is about 60% winners, while Pregame's current season table for all his rated picks is just under 50%. On the Watchdog board, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Spartan is very thin. The comments we found sit on the store that sells him or simply copy his plays. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found very little from buyers. The only praise sits on Pregame's own forum in Jan 2012, where a few members thanked him for playoff and Game of the Year winners. In Mar 2026 a member of the Bookmakers Review forum reposted one of his plays with a losing season count attached, without comment. CapperTek has a profile for him with no reviews at all, and our archive of Reddit betting posts held nothing about him. We found no complaint about billing, refunds or delivery, and no independent buyer reporting a profit or a loss.

In a Pregame forum thread tied to his profile, several members thanked him for winners, including a 49ers play and a Giants Game of the Year in the NFL playoffs. One said he regretted parlaying the 49ers with a losing Denver play. Pregame runs the forum and sells his picks, so this is not independent evidence, and it is old.

On the Bookmakers Review forum, a member posted his college basketball SEC tournament Game of the Year on Oklahoma along with a season college basketball record of 77 and 98 and 1. No one discussed the result.

CapperTek lists Spartan.pregame.com with no reviews or complaints. We found no Sportsbook Review, Covers or TheRX thread about his service, no Better Business Bureau profile, and no posts about him in our archive of r/sportsbook and r/sportsbetting posts. TheRX tells members not to post write ups from Pregame.

conflicts: Pregame sells his picks, grades them, keeps the record and runs the forum where buyers comment. That does not make the records wrong, but no outside party checks them.

His sales copy is written in the store's voice and calls the price "NEVER" this low again on several packages at once. Treat list prices such as $5,000 for a basketball season as marketing, not a real comparison.
strengths: Pregame publishes his graded record by sport and period, including losing categories, which most sellers do not.
Every package has a published price, and single plays let you sample him for $20.
Pregame states plainly that it sells no pick guarantee instead of dressing up store credit as one.
concerns: On Pregame's own tables his rated picks this season are just under 50% across all sports, with weighted losses in most sports.
The sales page leads with one strong category, NFL Triple Stars, rather than the overall record.
Claims such as two NBA championships at Free Sports Monitor and six winning NFL years out of seven are not dated or linked.
Flex Access rebills every month until you cancel by email.
Almost no independent buyer feedback exists, good or bad.
checklist: Look at the full graded record for every sport, not only the category in the headline.
Count units, not wins. A 60% record at heavy favorites can still lose money.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: Spartan is a real, long running seller on Pregame, a Las Vegas store with written terms and published prices. Pregame grades his picks in public. We found no court or regulator action involving him, and no independent check of his claimed contest titles.
On 17 Nov 2026 Pregame sold a single Spartan play for $20, 7 days for $119, 30 days for $249, 90 days for $449 and one year for $1,995. Season passes ran from $359 for NHL to $885 for all basketball.
Does Spartan have a verified record?

Pregame keeps a graded record, but Pregame also sells the picks, so it is not independent. On 17 Nov 2026 that record showed his rated picks this season at 488 wins and 492 losses across all sports, while his sales page highlighted an NFL Triple Star run of 277 and 183.

His top NFL plays have a long marketed run, but his overall rated record this season sits just under 50%, below the roughly 52.4% needed at -110. Pregame offers no pick guarantee, and nothing covers your betting losses.
